title: Turn your team's best client emails into social posts
metaTitle: Content ideas for IT firms: your sent folder
description: IT teams write careful emails to clients every day. Search the sent folder for the best answers and turn each one into a social post.
dek: Your next 10 social posts have already been written. They're in your consultants' sent folder.
author: Shane Kennedy

shortVersion: The team writes carefully worded emails to clients every day, and each one helps that one client, once.
Search the sent box for the best answers to the most complex questions, and pick five or six.
Take the client's details out, write a post around each, and get the rest of the team doing the same.

beats.heading: "We don't have time for content"
body: What I often hear from IT service businesses is that they don't have time for content. They're just so stuck in delivery.
That's fair. Client work pays the bills, and a social post can wait until next week. Meanwhile, the team is writing carefully worded emails to clients every single day.

beats.heading: Only one client sees it
body: Each of those emails helps that one client, once. The rest of your market doesn't see it.

Say someone on the team explained, in plain words, why a migration was taking longer than planned, or what a licence change would do to a client's bill. Another firm's got the same question this week, and there's no way for them to find that answer.

beats.heading: Search the sent box
body: So when you're planning your next batch of social posts, look at the sent box. Find the best responses to the most complex questions.
A search helps. Try long replies, and threads where a client's asked "how do" or "why". Start with the ones where the client was worried about something.

rows.subject: Re: How do we stop tickets piling up over the holidays?
Re: Why did last night's backup fail?
Re: How do we move our files off the old server?
Re: Why is the internet slow every afternoon?

beats.heading: Pick the best five or six
body: Pick the best five or six, where the gold is, and then write content around them.
Take the client's name out first, and anything else that'd identify them. The question and the answer are what's useful to the next reader, and they read just as well without the name.
And of course, Claude can help you. Paste in the answer, with the client's details already removed, and ask for a first draft of a post you can then edit.

steps.text: Search the sent box for the best answers
Pick the ones where the gold is
Write a post around each one

beats.heading: Ask the team for theirs
body: If you're looking for volume, you can get your team to do the exact same thing.
Ask each consultant to forward their best answer once a month. That can give you more material than you can post.
